title: Clinical Evaluation of aklaria for the Initial Diagnostic Assessment of Mental Health Disorders: A Vignette-based Study
summary:
aklaria is an online program for adults with mental health symptoms. It asks structured questions about common mental health conditions, such as depressive and anxiety disorders, and suggests possible suspected diagnoses. These suggestions are intended to support physicians and psychotherapists during the initial assessment. 
This study examines how accurate these suspected diagnoses are. Instead of real patient interviews, the study uses written case examples (vignettes). About 300 adults from the general population in Germany each read 6 case examples and enter the information into aklaria as if they were the person described. Participation is fully online. Participants are given two weeks to complete the tasks.
conditions: Case vignettes representing mental disorders from 10 ICD-10 categories.

interventions.name: All participants complete 6 standardised case vignettes in the online programme aklaria within 14 days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Consent to participate
• Sufficient knowledge of the German language
• Sufficient digital literacy skills to use aklaria independently
Exclusion criteria:
• Employee of the developing company/sponsor
• Acute psychological instability 
• Current pregnancy
• Currently breastfeeding
• aklaria contraindications assessable at screening:
  – Suicide-related risk
  – Psychotic symptoms
  – Insufficient language comprehension or cognitive inability to complete the task
